result.oban_signoff: AGREE with NO -- Oban is not adopted as a mix.exs dependency. Grounds 1 (scope mismatch against SCH-02's narrower specified behaviour), 3 (Oban's own attempt/retry counter would duplicate or have to be neutered against REQ-186's domain-specified fire_error_count/failed/DLQ machinery, ported bit-for-bit from R-Co's ISS-303 fix) and 4 (this project's own standing new-dependency-adoption precedent per decision 0003 and REQ-148) are each independently sufficient and are concurred with on their own terms. Ground 2 (tenant-scoping impedance against Decision 0003's schema-per-tenant model) is real but only partially dispositive alone -- Oban could in principle serve purely as a cluster-wide tick driver while the actual per-tenant FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claim query stays custom -- noted in the sign-off for a future reader, but it does not change the verdict since grounds 1/3/4 do not depend on it. Full sign-off text recorded in lib/letflow/design/req185-scheduler-firing-architecture.md section 3.
idiom_and_scope_findings: Supervision idiom confirmed: section 2b's supervised GenServer ticker plus a sixth scheduler-owned Task.Supervisor for per-tick fire attempts follows lib/letflow/application.ex's existing Task.Supervisor-per-concern idiom exactly (five such supervisors already exist: SandboxPool, Engine plugin, Lua, Wasm module registry, Wasm capability gate, Wasm module version registry) -- not a new supervision shape.

No decision in this artefact silently reopens or contradicts docs/migration/decisions/0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md Decision B -- section 6 explicitly treats Decision B as binding table placement only, correctly frames the poller's per-tenant-schema iteration strategy as the separate open question Decision B leaves unanswered, and rejects a global-queue design specifically because it would conflict with Decision B. Section 8's DLQ write path is correctly tenant-scoped consistent with Decision 0003's 2026-08-17 addendum.

No scope creep found -- the artefact is scope-disciplined: it declines to build query-cost mitigation machinery not yet needed (section 6, deferred as OQ-2), and part of the Oban rejection itself (section 3 point 1) is an explicit anti-scope-creep argument (Oban is more machinery than this requirement's scope calls for).

Non-blocking forward note for REQ-186 (not filed under docs/issues/ -- no new struct/schema/transition logic exists yet in this design-only artefact to file a type-safety gap against): REQ-186's own design should state explicitly which per-timer failure-isolation mechanism it uses (a Task.Supervisor process boundary per section 2b, a Repo.transaction/1 + rescue boundary per section 7, or both together), since this artefact describes each without stating whether both apply.
